items.title: Gojoseon & Ancient Bare-Handed Survival Combat
items.subtitle: 고조선 & 고대 생존 무예의 기원
items.body: In ancient times, children and adults were actively encouraged to learn bare-handed martial arts because combat techniques were essential for individual survival, hunting, and tribal community defense.
details: Martial arts served as a primary means of personal social advancement and national tribal survival.
Ritual martial tournaments were held during agricultural festivals such as Yeonggo and Dongmaeng.
Laid the cultural bedrock linking physical martial prowess with spiritual character cultivation.
Key Figures: Ancient Tribal Leaders, Frontier Cadets

items.title: Goguryeo Sun Bae Warriors & Muyongchong Tomb Murals
items.subtitle: 고구려 조의선인(선배) & 무용총 수박 벽화
items.body: Goguryeo formed the Sun Bae ("men of virtue who never recoil from fighting"), an elite warrior brotherhood tested at the annual Sin Su Do festival in Subak and archery.
details: Murals in the Myung-Chong (Muyongchong) royal tomb depict two martial artists sparring in upright stances.
Warriors studied classical literature, history, ethics, and martial combat simultaneously.
Subak served as the primary physical training foundation for northern frontier defense.
Key Figures: King Dongmyeong (Jumong), Sun Bae Elite Corps

items.title: Silla Hwarangdo & The Sesok-Ogye Five Commandments
items.subtitle: 신라 화랑도(花郞徒) & 세속오계(世俗五戒)
items.body: The kingdom of Silla established the Hwarang (Flower Knights), an aristocratic youth order trained in bare-handed Subak, swordcraft, and the Sesok-Ogye ethical commandments.
details: Sesok-Ogye: Loyalty to country, filial obedience, trust with friends, courage in battle, restraint in killing.
These five secular commandments became the direct moral foundation for the modern 5 Tenets of Taekwondo.
Hwarang military discipline catalyzed the historic unification of the Three Kingdoms of Korea.
Key Figures: Monk Won Gwang, General Kim Yu-sin, Hwarang Knights

items.title: Goryeo Dynasty Subakhui Military Examinations
items.subtitle: 고려시대 수박희(手搏戱) 무예 과거 제도
items.body: Historical chronicles of the Medieval Goryeo era specifically record the activities of Subak (Subakhee). The military formalized Subak as official testing for officer promotions.
details: Subak proficiency was mandatory for all royal bodyguard cadets protecting the king.
King Uijong and King Myeongjong hosted national tournaments in palace courtyards.
Distinguished martial artists were promoted directly to general and minister officer ranks.
Widely practiced not only by palace soldiers, but also celebrated as athletic folk games among the public.
Key Figures: King Uijong, General Yi Ui-min, Military Officers

items.title: Muyedobotongji Martial Arts Compendium by King Jeongjo
items.subtitle: 정조 1790년 무예도보통지(武藝圖譜通志) 편찬
items.body: King Jeongjo of the Joseon Dynasty commissioned the Muyedobotongji (Comprehensive Illustrated Manual of Martial Arts). Volume 4 "Kwonbeop" (fist method) detailed 38 bare-handed combat postures.
details: Kwonbeop chapter cataloged official linear punches, palm strikes, blocks, and footwork sequences.
Synthesized native Korean martial methods with Chinese General Qi Jiguang’s military combat texts.
Proves direct documentary lineage from traditional Korean unarmed combat into modern Taekwondo.
Key Figures: King Jeongjo, Scholar Lee Duk-moo, Baek Dong-soo

items.title: Japanese Occupation & Underground Taekkyeon Preservation
items.subtitle: 일제강점기 전통 무예의 탄압 & 태견의 맥 보존
items.body: During the 35-year Japanese colonial occupation, indigenous Korean martial arts were strictly suppressed. However, Taekkyeon and Subak were preserved underground in rural regions.
details: Grandmaster Song Deok-ki kept traditional Taekkyeon fluid footwork and rhythmic kicking alive in Inwangsan.
Korean students studying abroad in Japan and Manchuria learned Shotokan Karate and Northern Kung Fu.
This fusion created the explosive technical foundation for the opening of the Kwans after 1945 liberation.
Key Figures: Grandmaster Song Deok-ki, Underground Masters

items.title: Post-Liberation Opening of the Five Original Kwans
items.subtitle: 광복 직후 5대 기간관(基幹館) 개관
items.body: Immediately following Korea’s liberation, the original Five Kwans (Chung Do Kwan, Song Moo Kwan, Moo Duk Kwan, Jidokwan, Chang Moo Kwan) were established in Seoul, sparking the modern Taekwondo revolution.
details: Chung Do Kwan was established in 1944 by Grandmaster Lee Won-kuk as the first civil martial gym.
The Kwans began experimenting with bamboo chest protectors for full-contact dynamic sparring.
Emphasized high jumping kicks and fluid combinations distinct from rigid Japanese karate.
Key Figures: Lee Won-kuk, Ro Byung-jik, Hwang Kee, Chun Sang-sup, Yoon Byung-in

items.title: Official Naming & Adoption of "Taekwondo"
items.subtitle: 1955년 4월 11일 「태권도(跆拳道)」 명칭 제정
items.body: On April 11, 1955, a formal assembly of military leaders, kwan masters, and prominent scholars officially approved the unified name "Taekwondo" (Tae: kick/smash with foot; Kwon: fist/strike; Do: art/way of life).
details: The word "Tae" (跆) linked the art directly to ancient Taekkyeon while honoring kicking supremacy.
President Syngman Rhee bestowed executive calligraphy endorsing unified military and civil training.
Began the systemic phase-out of foreign terms like Tang Soo Do, Kong Soo Do, and Kwon Bop.
Key Figures: General Choi Hong-hi, Naming Committee Board

items.title: Korea Taekwondo Association (KTA) Unified Foundation
items.subtitle: 1961년 대한태수도협회(대한태권도협회) 창립
items.body: To resolve doctrinal divides among competing Kwans, the unified Korea Taekwondo Association (originally Korea Taesoodo Association) was founded on September 16, 1961.
details: Unified Dan rank testing protocols, certified instructor credentials, and tournament regulations.
Formed a technical committee to draft unified Poomsae patterns and standardize sparring rules.
Dispatched pioneer demonstration teams across Southeast Asia, Europe, and the Americas.
Key Figures: General Chae Myung-shin, Uhm Woon-kyu, Lee Jong-woo

items.title: Adoption as Official National Sports Festival Medal Sport
items.subtitle: 1963년 제44회 전국체육대회 공식 경기 종목 채택
items.body: At the 44th Korean National Sports Festival in Jeonju, Taekwondo was adopted as an official medal sport for the very first time, completing its transformation into an institutionalized modern athletic discipline.
details: Standardized the Hogu (chest protector) as mandatory safety gear for all competitive bouts.
Introduced formalized weight divisions and electronic round management systems.
Spurred Korean universities to establish academic Taekwondo science degree departments.
Key Figures: KTA Leadership, Korean Olympic Committee (KOC)

items.title: Presidential Calligraphy Declares "Kukki Taekwondo"
items.subtitle: 1971년 3월 20일 대통령 친필 휘호 「국기 태권도」 하사
items.body: On March 20, 1971, President Park Chung-hee personally penned and dedicated the official calligraphy "Kukki Taekwondo" (국기 태권도 - National Martial Art Taekwondo), establishing statutory sovereign patronage.
details: Unleashed executive government support to construct a permanent global headquarters in Seoul.
Mandated Taekwondo across public elementary, middle, and high school physical education.
Provided sovereign diplomatic backing for international embassy master postings.
Key Figures: President Park Chung-hee, Dr. Kim Un-yong

items.title: Kukkiwon (World Taekwondo Headquarters) Dedication
items.subtitle: 1972년 11월 30일 국기원(세계태권도본부) 개원
items.body: Kukkiwon was dedicated in Yeoksam-dong, Gangnam, Seoul as the central dojang of the world, serving as the sole authority for global Dan rank certifications and martial arts research.
details: Consolidated all private Kwan Dan certificates into one singular Kukkiwon Dan credential.
Established the World Taekwondo Academy (WTA) to license international master instructors.
Hosts the annual World Taekwondo Hanmadang, preserving the cultural core beyond Olympic sparring.
Key Figures: Dr. Kim Un-yong (Founding President)

items.title: World Taekwondo (WT) Founded & 1st World Championships
items.subtitle: 1973년 5월 28일 세계태권도연맹(WT) 창립 & 제1회 세계선수권
items.body: During the 1st World Taekwondo Championships at Kukkiwon, delegates from 19 nations founded the World Taekwondo Federation (WTF, now WT) to govern international sport competition.
details: Dr. Kim Un-yong was unanimously elected as the founding president of the federation.
Affiliated with GAISF (SportAccord) in 1975 to achieve international sporting legitimacy.
Unanimously recognized by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) at the 83rd session in 1980.
Key Figures: Dr. Kim Un-yong, Delegates from 19 Nations

items.title: IOC Unanimous Medal Sport Adoption at Paris Session
items.subtitle: 1994년 9월 4일 IOC 파리 총회 올림픽 정식 종목 채택
items.body: At the 103rd IOC Session in Paris, France, the International Olympic Committee voted unanimously to include Taekwondo as a full medal sport beginning at the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games.
details: September 4 was permanently designated as official "World Taekwondo Day" globally.
Capped triumphant demonstration debuts at the 1988 Seoul and 1992 Barcelona Olympic Games.
Became only the second Asian martial art in history to achieve full Olympic medal sport status.
Key Figures: Juan Antonio Samaranch (IOC President), Dr. Kim Un-yong

items.title: Olympic Medal Debut at Sydney 2000 Olympic Games
items.subtitle: 2000년 시드니 올림픽 정식 메달 종목 역사적 데뷔
items.body: Taekwondo made its historic debut as an official Olympic medal sport at the State Sports Centre in Sydney, Australia, featuring 103 competitors from 51 nations across 8 weight categories.
details: Gold medals were distributed across Europe, Asia, Americas, and Australasia, proving global parity.
Featured full gender equality with equal medal divisions for male and female athletes.
Introduced millions of global viewers to high-speed dynamic turning kicks.
Key Figures: Athletes from 51 Nations, WT International Referees

items.title: Statutory Law Designating Taekwondo as National Martial Art of Korea
items.subtitle: 2018년 3월 30일 국회 「태권도 국기(國技) 지정법」 법제화 통과
items.body: The National Assembly of the Republic of Korea passed a historic statutory amendment officially enshrining into statutory law: "The National Martial Art of the Republic of Korea shall be Taekwondo".
details: Elevated the cultural status from a customary tradition into legally protected sovereign national heritage.
Confirmed core Olympic status through Paris 2024, LA 2028, and Brisbane 2032.
Advanced transparent electronic PSS sensor scoring and 4D IVR instant video review.
Key Figures: National Assembly of Korea, Kukkiwon & WT Leadership
